subject: Field audit playbook: scope, remote inspection, SOC 2 assertions
messages:

Subject: Field audit playbook + SOC 2 assertions mapping for MSA security exhibit

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As we move toward finalizing the order form and Security Exhibit for our contract, Procurement asked that we align on two things before legal redlines: the field-audit/playbook approach (what "inspection" actually looks like) and a one-page mapping of your SOC 2 assertions to the Exhibit clauses.

High-level asks from Medica:
- Confirm whether on-site/remote inspection will be allowed and what controls are in-scope for a sampled inspection (encryption at rest, access logs, key management, incident response).
- A proposed evidence cadence (when we can expect SOC 2 artifacts, sampling windows, and a pen-test access window).
- Any restrictions on observers or non-technical reviewers during a field visit.

I've attached a short template (soc2-assertions-mapping_v1.xlsx) to help. Can your team propose a concise playbook and a 2-week window in August for a pen-test inspection if needed?

Thanks,
Anna Keller
ComplianceOps — Medica Health
(complianceops@medica.com)

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Field audit playbook + SOC 2 assertions mapping for MSA security exhibit

Anna — thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers up front:
- Remote inspection is our standard for hosted customers; we support on-site only for Dedicated or Private deployments and with an approved NDA/visitation plan.
- In-scope controls for sampling we normally include: system access controls (IAM), logging & monitoring (retention window and tracers), encryption at rest/in transit, vulnerability/pen test reports (redacted), and incident response evidence.
- Observers: we allow a single named technical observer; no vendors or press.

Action plan from Redwood:
1) We will fill your SOC2 mapping template and flag any assertion-to-clause gaps by EOD tomorrow.
2) Karthik will propose a pen-test window and scope; if you need on-site, we will outline the visitor security rules.
3) Laura will create a short playbook (3 pages) describing evidence handoff, sampling sizes, and remote inspection tech steps (screen-share + AWS/GCP console readouts via Zoom).

Proposed short timeline: initial mapping by 2027-07-21, playbook draft by 2027-07-23, and tentative pen-test window in Aug (2027-08-09 to 2027-08-20) — flexible if those dates don't work.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Anna / team — adding technical detail on the pen-test and inspection mechanics.

Pen-test access notes (Redwood default):
- For hosted customers we provide a staging environment and a scoped test harness (no access to production keys or live PII).
- For Dedicated/Private, we can support a short production-attached window but only with an Ops escort and pre-approved IP ranges.
- We require a pen-test plan 7 days in advance, with exploits limited to non-destructive tests unless otherwise authorized and with rollback steps documented.

Remote inspection mechanics:
- We prefer video-assisted console walkthroughs (Zoom with screenshare + session recording for the customer).
- Evidence transfer: SFTP to a Medica-designated bucket OR shared Drive link with MFA.
- Sampling: we typically request a sample of 10-20 artifacts per control (config snapshots, log extracts, account lists) for initial review.

I'll attach a short draft scope (pen-test-scope-draft.pdf) and propose the Aug 9–13 window first (narrower). If you really need on-site, we can discuss logistics and an approved visitor whitelist.

- Karthik

Thanks, Hannah and Karthik — this reads well. A few clarifying points from Procurement and Internal Security: 
- Medica strongly prefers remote-first inspections; on-site only if you require it for Dedicated/private and with a signed site-visit NDA.
- For evidence transfer we will use the SFTP option; please confirm a PGP fingerprint or an account to push to.
- Sampling: confirm whether the 10–20 artifact sample includes both configuration snapshots and log extracts (we prefer both).

Can Laura share the draft playbook by COB Friday (2027-07-23)? Procurement also asked for one sentence in the contract about the "observer" policy (single named, technical, no recording without consent).

Anna

Subject: Re: Field audit playbook + SOC 2 assertions mapping for MSA security exhibit

Anna — attaching the 3-page playbook draft and a one-line contract clause to drop into the Security Exhibit. Summary below and the Drive link in case you want to comment inline.

Quick summary of playbook (attached):
- Remote-first inspection flow: kickoff call -> artifact request list -> screen-share walkthrough -> evidence upload to SFTP -> follow-up Q&A.
- Sampling: 12 artifacts per control by default (mix of config snapshots + filtered log extracts); we list fallback sampling when log retention < requested window.
- Pen-test: staging-first by default; production window only for Dedicated/Private with Ops escort and write-blocks.
- Observers: "Customer may name one technical observer per inspection; recording requires written consent from Redwood."

Contract clause (suggested one-liner):
"Customer inspection rights shall be exercised remotely by default; on-site inspections require mutual written agreement and execution of a site-visit NDA. Customer may designate up to one named technical observer; recording of sessions is prohibited without Redwood's prior written consent."

If that looks good I will: 1) post the completed SOC 2 mapping workbook to the Drive, 2) circulate the final playbook for signature, and 3) add the pen-test window to the order form notes (DL-8943).

Laura Bennett
Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference
